title: Projected Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Flows for Hawkes Background-Intensity Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2610.19588v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the background intensity of a Hawkes process when the triggering mechanism is known, treating the background as an unknown finite positive measure with a regular density. We propose a likelihood-based variational approach based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry. In this setting, the relevant first variations are naturally distribution-valued and therefore fall outside the classical gradient-flow formulation. We develop a distributional framework for the resulting dynamics and give them a finite-dimensional meaning through projections onto statistical manifolds. We identify the true background as the unique zero of a limiting generalized gradient and, under suitable stability, compactness, integrability and approximation conditions, establish a conditional consistency theorem for measurable estimators satisfying the empirical projected equations on events whose probabilities tend to one. Finall

translated_title: 用于Hawkes过程背景强度估计的投影Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao流
translated_abstract: 我们考虑在触发机制已知的情况下估计Hawkes过程背景强度的问题，将背景视为一个具有正则密度的未知有限正测度。我们提出了一种基于Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao几何的似然变分方法。在这一设定下，相关的一阶变分天然地是分布取值的，因此超出了经典梯度流表述的范畴。我们为由此产生的动力学建立了一个分布框架，并通过向统计流形的投影赋予其有限维意义。我们将真实背景识别为极限广义梯度的唯一零点，并在适当的稳定性、紧性、可积性和逼近条件下，为在概率趋于1的事件上满足经验投影方程的可测估计量建立了条件一致性定理。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao几何的似然变分方法，通过向统计流形投影的分布框架来估计Hawkes过程的背景强度，并证明了相应估计量的条件一致性定理。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a likelihood-based variational approach using Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry, developing a distributional framework with projections onto statistical manifolds to estimate the background intensity of Hawkes processes, and establishing a conditional consistency theorem for the resulting estimators.
